page: Amazon Web Services i4g.xlarge is a storage-optimized cloud instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The system features 4 dedicated AWS Graviton Neoverse-N1 cores operating at 2.5 GHz on the 64-bit ARMv8 architecture. Each vCPU represents a dedicated physical core with single-threaded execution, backed by 64 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. Memory capacity is configured at 32 GB, providing 8 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware accelerators are absent, with zero GPUs included. Local high-speed storage is bundled directly via a 937 GB NVMe solid-state drive, accompanied by a 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth.

Benchmark measurements highlight consistent base computation alongside lower single-thread instruction throughput. Synthetic stress-ng evaluations place both single-core (1520.08) and multi-core (6056.47) results within the middle 50% performance bracket. Uncached large-block memory read bandwidth reaches 71.67 GB/sec, with write bandwidth achieving 34.86 GB/sec. Geekbench single-core (969.0) and multi-core (3224.0) scores register in the bottom quartile, matched by modest scores in Clang software compilation and PassMark system testing. Hardware cryptographic capabilities include AES, whereas advanced matrix and vector extensions are not supported.

The hardware design of the i4g.xlarge reflects clear operational tradeoffs. Pairing custom ARM silicon with an integrated 937 GB NVMe drive provides efficient resource utilization for storage-centric services relative to decoupled network block storage. While single-thread instruction throughput and network baseline speed are modest, the 8 GB per vCPU ratio and local disk throughput yield strong architectural efficiency for data-heavy profiles.

Given its storage density and memory capacity, the instance is well suited for localized relational and NoSQL databases, in-memory caching like Redis, log ingestion pipelines, and search index services requiring low-latency NVMe access without the requirement for x86-specific instruction sets.
description: Amazon Web Services i4g.xlarge is a storage-optimized virtual instance powered by 4 dedicated AWS Graviton Neoverse-N1 cores based on the 64-bit ARMv8 architecture running at 2.5 GHz. Built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, the instance supplies 32 GB of system memory, providing an 8 GB per vCPU ratio, alongside a bundled 937 GB local NVMe SSD and a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps. It does not include dedicated graphics processing units. In performance benchmarks, the processor demonstrates average stress-ng single-core and multi-core throughput, while complex integer, text processing, and single-threaded compilation metrics rank in lower percentiles. Memory bandwidth yields 71.67 GB/sec for uncached read operations. The instance architecture trades raw compute intensity for local storage capability and balanced memory density. It is suitable for I/O-dependent applications, localized database operations, Redis caching layers, and search index nodes requiring fast direct NVMe disk access without requiring high-frequency x86 processing cores.
